newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka refinery output seen back fully next wee.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka refinery output seen back fully next wee.

text.p: Production at Sri Lanka's only oil refinery should be back to normal by the end of this week or early next week, after a routine maintenance shutdown, a spokesman said on Monday.
"We're now starting to get the first units going," he said. "It will take seven or eight days or even longer."
The 60,000 barrels-per-day Sapugaskanda refinery, located just north of the capital Colombo and run by the state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC), was shut down for maintenance on January 15.
During the shutdown, CPC imported a total of 200,000 tonnes of gas oil, jet fuel and gasoline, the spokesman said.
